name: TX-11
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a +17 Republican partisan lean
Incumbent August Pfluger running with a large financial advantage ($3.2M raised vs $89K)
No polls or expert ratings; prediction markets price the Democrat at about 4%
model.rationale: The district's +17 Republican lean, Pfluger's incumbency and roughly 35-to-1 fundraising edge, and markets pricing the Democrat near 4% all point to a safe Republican hold. No polls or ratings suggest any reason to move materially off that picture.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or unexpectedly weak Republican turnout in a low-salience race could narrow the margin, though a flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
West Texas's 11th District is solidly Republican territory, and two-term incumbent August Pfluger is seeking reelection after easily winning the nomination. He enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised about $3.2 million and holding $2.9 million on hand, while Democrat Claire Reynolds has raised under $100,000 with no outside support on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Reynolds only about a 4% chance of winning. With the district's strong Republican lean and Pfluger's incumbency advantage, the seat is rated Safe Republican, with Reynolds needing an exceptional and unlikely shift to make it competitive.
